summary: This is a corrective fix-forward on PR #596 that closes a real audit-confirmed FAIL (interim/RA bills posting with silent $0 GST because no invoice line ever carried a taxTemplateId, and a negative 'Retention held' invoice line that additionally shrank the taxable subtotal). The fix requires and validates a real taxTemplateId belonging to the org before generating a bill, extracts a pure computeInvoiceTaxTotals() out of the existing computeInvoiceTotals() in erp-invoicing-service.ts, and removes the negative retention line in favor of billing the full gross value with retention tracked only as a separate holdback (constructionInterimBills.retentionAmount/netPayable) -- which is the correct GST treatment (tax is due on certified work value regardless of retention terms). New unit tests directly assert nonzero tax on real rates and that the taxable subtotal no longer shrinks from a synthetic negative line. The hand-written migration (renumbered 0265->0267 to resolve a post-merge collision) matches schema.ts exactly, follows the established RLS pattern from 0101_wave115 (direct org_id policy on construction_interim_bills, EXISTS-join policy via parent on the line-items table), and the new 0265_snapshot.json is a verified-accurate drizzle baseline. No changes touch .github/workflows/**. Governance files (ACTIVE-CLAIMS, registry exemptions) are updated consistently with the actual diff. The one known gap -- billNumber assigned via a read-then-insert race -- is pre-existing convention elsewhere in this codebase and explicitly out of scope, not a regression. This is correctly tier2 (schema/migration touched) and should proceed to human sign-off before the migration is applied to any live Supabase project, since that step (and the resulting get_advisors(security) run) has not happened yet.
issues: Migration drizzle/0267_construction_boq_hierarchy_interim_billing.sql has not been applied to any live Supabase project yet -- get_advisors(security) has not been run against the new tables' real RLS; this must happen as part of (or right after) human sign-off, not be assumed safe from hand-verification alone.

billNumber is assigned via a max(billNumber)+1 read-then-insert with no unique constraint or advisory lock, so two concurrent interim-bill generations for the same project could collide -- acknowledged by the author as a pre-existing convention (erpSalesInvoices.invoiceNumber has the same pattern) and explicitly out of this task's scope, not a new regression, but worth a follow-up ticket.
